title: The Ultimate Horse Transport Checklist: Travel Safe & Prepared
summary: Loading up for a competition, training clinic, or trip to the coast is one of the most exciting parts of horse ownership. However, travelling with horses comes with inherent risks. Proper transport preparation ensures a smooth journey for both rider and horse.
metaDescription: Heading out to a show or hack? Review our essential horse transport checklist to keep your horse safe on the road.

sections.heading: 1. Perform Pre-Trip Horsebox & Trailer Safety Checks
paragraphs: Before loading your horse, run through a quick 5-minute safety check:
list: Flooring: Lift rubber mats regularly to check timber or aluminium floors for rot, weakness, or corrosion.
Tyres: Check tyre pressure and tread depth (including the spare tyre!). Tyres deteriorate over time, even with low mileage.
Hitch & Lights: Ensure the breakaway cable, trailer hitch, and all exterior brake/indicator lights are fully functioning.
Dates & Paperwork: Keep track of your vehicle's breakdown cover, MOT, and servicing schedules so you aren't stranded far from home.

sections.heading: 2. Pack an Equine Travel First Aid Kit
paragraphs: Your transport kit should always include essential emergency supplies kept in an easily accessible compartment:
list: Cohesive bandages (Vetrap) and sterile non-stick dressings
Instant cold packs for sudden swelling

sections.heading: 3. Secure Vital Details on the Road
paragraphs: If an accident or breakdown occurs while you are towing, emergency services or rescue crews need immediate access to your horse's information and your breakdown membership details.

Having a physical record inside the vehicle - or a digital travel tag attached to your horsebox or equipment - allows first responders to contact your emergency keyholders, identify breakdown insurance details, and access your horse's medical background instantly.
sections.tip: Travel with Confidence: Products like NeighTag allow horse owners to link breakdown policies, insurance info, and emergency contacts to a scan-ready QR code attached directly to your horsebox or trailer gear.

sections.heading: 4. Monitor Horse Comfort & Hydration
list: Offer fresh water every 2 to 3 hours during long trips to prevent dehydration and impaction colic.
Ensure adequate ventilation without creating high-speed draughts inside the horse compartment.
Use suitable leg protection (travel boots or bandages) only if your horse is accustomed to them to prevent shipping injuries.
